name: Gauley River Rafting
unique: Twenty five miles of continuous Class IV–V whitewater fed by controlled dam releases for a few weeks each September, the biggest commercial whitewater in the East.
buzz: Guides call it the real thing; the Upper Gauley is not for beginners and swimming is a serious proposition. Book as soon as the schedule drops.

name: New River Gorge Whitewater
unique: The Lower New has the biggest consistent whitewater in the East and a gorge lined with hundred-foot cliffs; the Upper New is a gentler float through the same scenery.
buzz: Outfitters are rated on guide quality, not just the rapids; the full day Lower New is the consensus classic. Water is cold and the hike out is real.

name: Bridge Day on the New River Gorge
unique: One day a year the 876-foot New River Gorge Bridge closes to cars and opens to base jumpers, hundreds of them, legally, into a national park.
buzz: Even non-jumpers rate it a spectacle; traffic is a nightmare and the walk out to the catwalk is the best view. Vendors are fairground grade.

name: Hatfield McCoy Trails
unique: Hundreds of miles of interconnected trail systems through former coal country, with towns that allow ATVs on the streets and trailheads that connect to food and lodging.
buzz: This is the benchmark for eastern off roading: well marked, well maintained and enormous. Book a cabin and plan two days minimum.

name: Dolly Sods Wilderness
unique: A high plateau that looks like subarctic tundra, wind-stunted spruce, blueberry heath and boulder fields, hundreds of miles south of where it should be.
buzz: Hikers call it the strangest landscape in the East and warn about mud, fog and unmarked trails. Wear boots you don't love.

name: Harpers Ferry
unique: The confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah, where John Brown raided the arsenal and the Appalachian Trail walks straight through a preserved 19th century town.
buzz: The Lower Town is beautifully preserved and the Maryland Heights hike is the payoff; parking is a shuttle ride away.

name: Moundsville State Penitentiary
unique: A Gothic prison with a working gallows, a recreation of the electric chair and a subterranean cell block called the hole, offering day tours and overnight ghost hunts.
buzz: Guides are former guards and tell unvarnished stories; the overnight events are not for everyone. One of the most intense prison tours in the country.

name: Seneca Rocks
unique: A 900-foot quartzite fin rising out of the Potomac Highlands, with a knife edge hiking trail to the summit and multi-pitch trad routes up the face.
buzz: Climbers call it the best trad venue in the East; the hiking trail is exposed and genuinely scary for some. The via ferrata guide service gets good reviews.

name: Greenbrier Bunker Tour
customer: History buffs, Cold War nerds, retirees
unique: A declassified underground bunker built to shelter Congress from nuclear war, hidden behind a resort for thirty years with a fake exhibition hall as its door.
buzz: The tour is fascinating and slightly eerie; guides are excellent on the secrecy. The resort itself is a time capsule worth a drink at the bar.

name: Babcock State Park Grist Mill
unique: A working water powered grist mill with a red roof over a mossy creek, surrounded by rhododendron and the New River Gorge, the most photographed mill in the state.
buzz: Photographers queue at dawn for the mill and the creek; the park cabins are a quiet base for gorge hiking. Autumn is the peak.

name: Beckley Exhibition Coal Mine
unique: Ride a mantrip cart into a real worked coal seam with a former miner as your guide, then walk a recreated company town of shacks, church and school.
buzz: The miner guides are the whole experience, funny, blunt and full of detail. The tour is cool underground even in August.

name: Cass Scenic Railroad
unique: Shay geared steam locomotives haul you up a logging railroad to Bald Knob, the third-highest point in the state, through a company town frozen in 1900.
buzz: Rail fans love the sound of the Shays; the ride is long and slow, which is the point. Bring a jacket, the summit is cold.

name: Coopers Rock State Forest
unique: A sandstone overlook above the Cheat River gorge with a cliff edge view, plus miles of trails, climbing and a CCC picnic shelter.
buzz: The overlook is the photograph and the underlook trail is the adventure; the forest is busy in fall and the cliffs are for experienced climbers.

name: Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum
unique: A vast Gothic Revival asylum built on the Kirkbride plan, with a preserved ECT room, patient art and overnight ghost hunts in the wards.
buzz: The historical day tour is stronger than the ghost stuff; guides tell unvarnished stories of institutional abuse. The building is enormous.

name: Berkeley Springs State Park
unique: A warm spring bathhouse in the middle of a small town, used since before the Revolution, with private baths and a Roman bath house.
buzz: The baths are the reason to come and the town is full of spas and shops; George Washington bathed here and the water is still free at the fountain.

name: Blennerhassett Island
unique: A island in the Ohio River reached by sternwheeler, with a reconstruction of the mansion Aaron Burr visited and a horse drawn wagon tour.
buzz: The sternwheeler ride and the mansion are the reasons to go and the island is flat and shaded; the tour runs on a schedule.

name: Durbin and Greenbrier Valley Railroad
unique: Heritage trains from Elkins into the Monongahela high country, with a dinner train, a wilderness train and a climb to the High Falls of the Cheat.
buzz: The wilderness train and the fall color are the reasons to book and the dinner train is the date night; seats go early in October.

name: Keith Albee Theater
unique: A 1928 Moorish Revival movie palace with a ceiling of clouds and castles, restored and used for concerts, films and touring shows.
buzz: The restoration alone is worth the ticket; sightlines are good from most seats. A grand room in a town people underestimate.

name: Summersville Lake
unique: The clearest lake in the state, with sandstone cliffs rising from the water that are a eastern climbing destination and a beach at the state park.
buzz: Climbers come for the overhanging sandstone and families come for the swim; the lake is deep and the cliffs are for experienced climbers only.

name: Lost World Caverns
unique: A self guided walk through a huge single chamber with a 45-foot stalagmite called the War Club, plus a wild-cave tour that crawls and gets muddy.
buzz: The self guided format lets you linger; the wild tour is the adventure. Small, cheap and genuinely impressive.

name: Mothman Festival
unique: A town leans into its own cryptid: a museum, a metal statue, guest speakers, a 5K and vendors selling moth-shaped everything, all in the shadow of the Silver Bridge disaster.
buzz: It is sincere, cheap and surprisingly wholesome; visitors love the museum and the parade. Parking is easier than you'd think.

name: Oglebay
unique: A 1,700 acre municipal resort with a glass museum, a zoo, golf and a winter Festival of Lights that draws busloads from three states.
buzz: The lights display is the regional tradition; the glass museum is the surprise. Good value for a family day.

name: Taylor Books
unique: An independent bookshop with a cafe and an art gallery upstairs, in a downtown that has lost most of its retail, and it is still busy on a Tuesday night.
buzz: The staff picks are good and the coffee is better than it needs to be; readings and live music most weeks.

name: Cacapon Resort State Park
unique: Six thousand acres on Cacapon Mountain with a lodge, a lake, horseback trails and a ridge trail to a view of three states.
buzz: The ridge trail and the lake are the reasons to come and the lodge is a good base; the park is quiet compared with the gorge.

name: Pricketts Fort
unique: A reconstructed palisade fort and cabins on the Monongahela, with interpreters in period dress and a 1770s job of work going on.
buzz: The fort and the demonstrations are the family draw and the site is on the river; the living history weekends bring it alive.

name: West Virginia Independence Hall
company: West Virginia Division of Culture and History
unique: The custom house where the Restored Government of Virginia met and the debate over West Virginia statehood happened, with the original courtroom and chambers.
buzz: The room where statehood was argued is the reason to come and it is free; the building is a cast iron fronted landmark in downtown Wheeling.

name: Core Arboretum
unique: Ninety one acres of old growth forest on the Monongahela river bluff with a trail system and a spring wildflower display, free on the university campus.
buzz: The spring wildflowers and the old trees are the reason naturalists come and it is free; the trails are steep in places.

name: Mountain State Forest Festival
unique: A festival of the state's timber heritage with lumberjack competitions, a parade, a queen and a sawdust pile for children, in the heart of the Monongahela forest.
buzz: The lumberjack contests are the draw and the parade is the tradition; it is a real county fair atmosphere with no tourists.

name: Oil and Gas Museum
unique: A museum of the oil and gas boom that started in this valley, with drilling tools, a model derrick and the stories of the wildcatters.
buzz: The tools and the photographs are the reason to stop; it is small and the volunteers know the local wells.

name: West Virginia Botanic Garden
unique: A garden on a former reservoir site with a wetland boardwalk, a children's garden and trails through woods, free to the public.
buzz: The boardwalk and the children's garden are the family stops and it is free; the garden is young and growing.
